project.name: CSV Import Assistant
project.objective:
A small B2B SaaS platform lets administrators upload CSV files containing customer contacts. They need a preview-and-validation workflow before importing contacts, to prevent invalid records from entering the customer database and to explain validation errors clearly.

The CSV import feature must:
1. Allow administrators to upload a CSV file.
2. Display a preview of the imported records.
3. Validate required fields.
4. Identify duplicate contacts within the uploaded file.
5. Display row-specific validation errors.
6. Allow administrators to confirm valid records before import.
7. Provide an import summary.

Every contact must have a valid email address. Rows with missing or invalid email addresses must be rejected.
project.constraints: Out of scope: production database integration, real customer information, authentication, external SaaS integrations, deployment, a complete CRM. Keep each document concise (under ~900 words).
project.success_criteria: An engineering team could build and test the CSV import workflow from these documents without further clarification.

1. Allow administrators to upload a CSV file.

3. Validate required fields.
4. Identify duplicate contacts within the uploaded file.
5. Display row-specific validation errors.
6. Allow administrators to confirm valid records before import.
7. Provide an import summary.

Every contact must have a valid email address. Rows with missing or invalid email addresses must be rejected.
Out of scope: production database integration, real customer information, authentication, external SaaS integrations, deployment, a complete CRM. Keep each document concise (under ~900 words).

messages.content: Update the CSV validation requirements. A customer contact may now be imported without an email address if a valid phone number is provided. Reject a row only if both contact methods are absent or invalid. Update the affected requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and QA tests.
Recorded the change. Upcoming tasks will follow it. I've listed the completed tasks it may affect — choose which to rework.

risks: If required contact fields beyond email are assumed inconsistently, engineering may implement unnecessary validation rules.
CSV edge cases such as malformed headers, empty rows, encoding issues, or very large files may need explicit handling guidance to avoid ambiguity.
Because production database integration is out of scope, import confirmation behavior must be framed clearly to avoid confusion between validated import simulation and persistence.
plan.scope: Define the CSV upload, preview, validation, duplicate detection within the uploaded file, row-specific error display, valid-record confirmation, and import summary workflow for administrator use. Documentation will explicitly require rejection of rows with missing or invalid email addresses and will stay within the stated constraints and out-of-scope boundaries.

tasks.title: Draft concise product and delivery requirements package
tasks.objective: Produce concise, implementation-ready documentation covering product requirements, prioritized user stories, and testable acceptance criteria for the CSV import workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Defines the end-to-end administrator workflow from CSV upload through confirmation and import summary.
Covers all required feature capabilities: upload, preview, required-field validation, duplicate detection within file, row-specific errors, confirm valid records, and import summary.
States that every contact must have a valid email address and that rows with missing or invalid email addresses are rejected.
Includes prioritized user stories with clear business value and scope boundaries.
Includes testable acceptance criteria sufficient for engineering and QA to build and verify without further clarification.
Keeps the document concise and under the requested length guideline.

tasks.title: Produce technical feasibility and risk assessment
tasks.objective: Assess implementation feasibility, key technical decisions, assumptions, and delivery risks for the CSV import workflow within the stated scope constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Explains a feasible implementation approach for CSV parsing, preview generation, validation flow, duplicate detection within the uploaded file, and import confirmation.
Identifies assumptions and constraints resulting from out-of-scope items such as no production database integration or deployment.
Highlights key risks, edge cases, and mitigation recommendations relevant to engineering implementation.
Aligns with the documented product requirements and does not expand scope.
Keeps the document concise and under the requested length guideline.

plan.summary: Create a concise statement of work to produce build-ready documentation for a CSV Import Assistant workflow: requirements, prioritized stories, acceptance criteria, and a technical feasibility/risk assessment, with independent QA review and final consolidation handled by the system.
assumptions: The import workflow is specified for administrator users only and does not require authentication design.
The output documents describe expected system behavior and validation rules, not production persistence or live integrations.
Duplicate detection is limited to duplicates found within a single uploaded CSV file, as stated in the requirements.
At minimum, email is a required field; any additional required fields will only be included if necessary to make the workflow internally consistent without expanding scope.
The final consolidated deliverable and QA review report will be generated by the system from the task outputs.
plan.budget_notes: Minimal two-task plan to keep scope tight: one business requirements package and one technical feasibility/risk assessment. QA review is enabled because the deliverables are intended to be build-ready and ambiguity would reduce their value.
out_of_scope: A complete CRM or broader contact-management functionality
acceptance_criteria: All requested deliverables are covered by the planned work and system-managed QA/final consolidation.
The resulting documents remain concise, within the stated scope, and under the requested length guideline per document.
An engineering team could implement and test the CSV import workflow from the deliverables without further clarification.
No out-of-scope functionality is specified as required implementation.
clarification_questions: Should duplicate detection treat email address comparison as case-insensitive and trimmed of surrounding whitespace?
Is the intended import result a simulated in-scope outcome (for example, a staged in-memory import summary) rather than any persistent write, given database integration is out of scope?
Should the preview show all parsed rows including invalid ones, or only rows eligible for confirmation?
